THE DAILY METALS PULSE ⚡
#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper
November 12 | Asia → Europe

A stronger dollar is squeezing metals again. But beneath the price action, the physical supply story remains worth watching.

🌏 ASIA: Chip stocks led losses after Nvidia’s sharp after-hours slide. Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury trading resumed after Veterans Day, with the 10-year yield near 5%. Higher borrowing costs and growing Fed hike expectations are keeping markets on edge.

☢️ URANIUM: This week’s demand backdrop keeps building. China began construction of San’ao unit 4 on Tuesday, while unit 2 completed fuel loading last week ahead of planned electricity supply in 2027. New reactors turn long-term nuclear ambitions into future fuel requirements.

🥈 SILVER: Around $51.37/oz, down roughly 0.3% in the morning snapshot. My focus today: whether silver can hold above $51 if the dollar strengthens further.

🥇 GOLD: Around $3,960/oz, down roughly 0.7%. Inflation anxiety is currently translating into higher rate expectations—a difficult combination for bullion. Watch Treasury yields closely.

🔶 COPPER: China’s physical market remains tight despite the macro pressure. SHFE inventories fell 24% in the week to November 6, while the Yangshan import premium held at a record $230/tonne yesterday. Metal availability and financial-market sentiment are telling different stories.

⏰ TODAY’S WATCHLIST — CET
• 14:30: U.S. weekly jobless claims.
• 16:00: Existing-home sales and Fed Governor Barr.
• 19:00: $25bn U.S. 30-year Treasury auction.
• Fed commentary throughout the day; Williams at 00:30 tonight.
• Friday’s U.S. PPI is the next major inflation test.

My take: today’s immediate driver is the dollar-and-yields reaction. Softer claims or strong Treasury demand could offer relief; another push higher in yields would keep metals under pressure.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the next pulse.

Jensen Huang’s resignation ends an era at NVIDIA and forces a stress test on the AI trade.

Huang wasn’t just a CEO. He was the face, the product visionary and the operator who turned NVIDIA into the $4T+ foundation of the AI boom. Key-man risk was always priced in at some level; today it is no longer theoretical. $NVDA stock is already down hard (10%+ in premarket) and the rest of the AI complex is feeling the spillover.

The near-term picture is messy. Leadership uncertainty, succession questions and the China-related overhang from the scandal create real noise. Colette Kress (long-time CFO, now interim CEO) and the existing leadership team provide operational continuity and the board has appointed Harvey Jones as its first Chair. Product roadmaps, CUDA lock-in and hyperscaler demand don’t disappear overnight. Still, the narrative premium from $NVDA is gone.

The setup for a multi-week rally is strong. AI stocks were already deeply oversold coming into this news after the recent sharp selloff. Technicals are washed out, sentiment is depressed and multiple strategists had already called the prior dip extreme. Forced selling and panic often exhaust quickly in these regimes. A relief bounce across the AI complex over the next several weeks looks highly probable as the dust settles.

The multi-month view is more nuanced. The AI infrastructure buildout itself is not over. Capex remains massive, data-centre demand is still the dominant growth driver and the underlying technology stack (accelerated computing, inference, networking) continues to expand. What changes is that NVIDIA must now prove it can execute without its founder-CEO narrative. Succession clarity, any regulatory/export fallout and whether the next permanent CEO can maintain the same cultural and technical intensity will decide if this is a healthy reset or the start of a longer period of relative underperformance versus the broader AI complex.

This is a classic “sell the rumor / buy the fact” environment for the trade. Oversold conditions favour a multi-week bounce. The multi-month case for AI stocks rests on whether the structural demand story can remain intact and companies with high margins, FCF and strong balance-sheets are likely to outperform. https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

The world is not ready for a swarm of agents. Everything will explode from infra (CI, Git, API) to the token consumption.

Today most people still work with one agent, one prompt at a time. But that agent can already spawn subagents, move to the cloud and run for hours, and stay on in the background 24/7. 

The next step is one agent starting a thousand others, and then swarms that never stop. Each step multiplies token consumption, and by the end we are talking about something like 10,000x what a single agent burns today. 

IMO nothing we built was sized for this. Git was designed for humans pushing a few times a day, CI for a handful of builds, APIs for a human rate of requests. A swarm breaks all of it at once. We need a new infrastructure, built for swarms of agents.
